agency.name: Texas Health and Human Services Commission (HHSC)

narrNote: Confirmed on NARR's official affiliates page (narronline.org/affiliates), which states verbatim that the Texas Recovery Oriented Housing Network (TROHN) is a founding state affiliate of the National Alliance for Recovery Residences (NARR). TROHN is a subsidiary of RecoveryPeople, certifies Texas recovery residences to the NARR standard (certification is voluntary under Texas law), and publishes a searchable certified recovery-housing directory on its own site, verified live in this run.
notes: HHSC is Texas's SAMHSA-designated Single State Agency for substance use; its Mental Health and Substance Use hub (fetched and content-verified in this run) lists adult substance use services: withdrawal management, intensive and supportive residential treatment, outpatient treatment, medication-assisted treatment, and peer support. The agency phone is the HHS state-office main number published on the official Texas DSHS contact page. LOCAL GATEWAY - OSAR: HHSC funds Outreach, Screening, Assessment and Referral (OSAR) programs across all 11 HHS regions; OSAR is the free first point of contact for substance-use screening, assessment, and referral into state-funded treatment, organized by region and the counties each program serves (all 254 Texas counties). HHSC publishes an OSAR directory on hhs.texas.gov (attested by multiple secondary sources), but the directory page's exact URL could not be surfaced by search in this run and URLs are never guessed, so countyDirectory is null rather than asserted unverified; the verified routes into OSAR are the HHSC hub above and 2-1-1 Texas, which HHSC itself operates (dial 2-1-1 or 877-541-7905). Crisis care in Texas is delivered locally through local mental health / behavioral health authorities (LMHAs/LBHAs), each with its own hotline; HHSC's statewide crisis entry point is its official 988 page (call or text 988). Medicaid: Texas Medicaid does cover substance use disorder treatment (assessment, outpatient counseling including MAT, residential treatment, withdrawal management) under HHSC rule 1 TAC 354.1311 and the Texas Medicaid Provider Procedures Manual, but no single official consumer-facing HHSC Medicaid SUD page could be verified in this run, so medicaidSud is null. Via Hope, historically Texas's statewide peer-specialist training and certification body, announced on its own site that it ceased operations effective 2025-08-01; it was therefore excluded from peerOrgs as a stale entry. BACKFILL 2026-10-22: a second pass worked from the verified HHSC hub and searched the official hhs.texas.gov domain for both open fields. Texas DSHS's own school-health resource document references an 'HHSC OSAR webpage,' but the page itself could not be located on the current hhs.texas.gov site in this pass, and no consumer-facing HHSC Medicaid SUD benefits page exists on the official domain (SUD coverage is documented in the Texas Medicaid Provider Procedures Manual and 1 TAC 354.1311 and delivered through managed-care plans). Per the never-guess rule, countyDirectory and medicaidSud remain null; the verified routes into OSAR remain the HHSC hub above and 2-1-1 Texas.
